title: Fold a pizza box from its flat blank: break in the side walls, lock the roll-over front on their tabs, shut the lid
instruction: Fold this pizza box from its flat blank and close it: lock the front wall over the side walls' tabs, then shut the lid with all three of its flaps inside. Leave the closed box on the board and let go.
context: Pizza is one of the most familiar take-out foods (USDA's dietary survey: "About 1 in 8 Americans consumed pizza on any given day"), and take-out and delivery pizza travels in a box like this one. Most people have opened and closed one at home, and the stack of flat blanks being folded behind a pizza shop's counter is a common sight (this box's listing: "It ships flat to maximize storage space and can easily be assembled by folding along perforated edges and locking the ends"). Anyone watching can tell whether the result is a box: walls up, front locked, lid shut. Each fold is held only by the next one. A side wall folded to upright and let go springs back down; folded on past upright, its score is broken in and it stays up. The front wall stays up once it is rolled over the side walls' tabs with its two feet in the base's slots. The lid stays shut once its three flaps are inside the walls. A tab left outside the roll-over gives a box that opens when it is picked up.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. A 61 cm length of 2x8 lumber (3.8 thick, 18.4 wide) lies flat on the table, clamped, long way along x: x 24.8 to 85.8, y -9.2 to 9.2. On it, inside face up and front toward the robot, lies one flat die-cut blank of a 10 x 10 x 2 in white corrugated pizza box (B flute, 3.2 mm thick; about 119 g; 69.4 long, 35.6 wide when flat). The board is narrower than the blank and starts 1.5 behind the box's front crease, so the front wall and its roll-over, both side walls, their tabs and the lid's side flaps hang over the board's edges. The blank's 13 panels, front to back: the inner leaf (24.7 wide, 4.7 deep) with two feet (2.6 wide, 0.65 long, centred 7.0 either side of the centre line); a 0.8 cap strip; the front wall (25.3 x 5.1); the base (25.4 x 25.4, centre at (36.0, 0), front crease at x 23.3) with two slots (4.0 x 0.74, 0.46 behind the front crease, centred 7.0 either side); the back wall (25.3 x 5.1); the lid (23.7 long, 24.6 wide); the lid's front flap (22.0 wide, 4.0 deep). Each side of the base: a side wall (24.4 long, 5.1 high) with a tab at its front end (5.8 long, 4.4 high). Each side of the lid: a side flap (16.2 long, 4.8 high, from 3.0 in front of the lid's hinge to 4.5 short of its front edge). Folded, the box is 25.4 x 25.4 x 5.1. Scores: a side wall, the front wall or the back wall folded up 90 degrees and let go comes back to about 65 degrees; once a wall has been folded past upright it rests that many degrees further up (folded to 125, it comes back to about upright). The short scores (tabs, cap, leaf, flaps) stay where they are put. Both arms start in their rest pose. Layout B (BOX_LOT=B): the blank and board 0.6 to the right.
scoring: Scored at the end, from how the box stands then (a ruler, a protractor or phone level, a photo). 0.25: both side walls up (within 30 degrees of upright) and the front wall's inner leaf rolled over at least one tab (the tab's free end lies between the front wall and the leaf). 0.5: the front is locked and holds by itself: both tabs under the roll-over, both feet in their slots (each foot's end at least 1 mm below the base's top face, so no foot shows above the base), the two side walls and the front wall each within 8 degrees of upright, and no gripper within 3 cm of them. 0.75: locked, and the lid is down (its front edge within 2 cm of the height of the walls' tops) but not shut, or a flap is outside, or a gripper is within 3 cm of the box, or something still moves. 1.0: locked; the lid shut (front edge within 6 mm of the walls' tops, level within 5 degrees, back wall within 10 degrees of upright); all three flaps inside the walls; both grippers at least 3 cm from the box; nothing moving (two video frames half a second apart). 0: anything else, including doing nothing, walls up with no tab under the roll-over, and a box that ends off the board. Sliding, turning or tipping the box on the board costs nothing.
reset_notes: Open the lid, pull the front wall's feet out of the slots, unroll it, and press the blank flat again, inside face up, at its marks on the board. A blank's scores are broken in after its first fold (its walls then stand without the pre-break), so use a new blank for every trial; one trial uses up one blank.
fidelity: Board modelled as 13 rigid 3.2 mm panels on 12 hinge lines; panels do not bend or twist, real board skews and dents. Each score is a spring with holding friction; the main scores take a set when folded past upright (one degree per degree, an estimate, as are all crease torques). From the listing: 10 x 10 x 2 in, B flute, ships flat, locks at the ends. Estimated: tab, slot, cap, flap and foot sizes (no die line published), mass, friction. Not tried on a real blank.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers reached the blank's side panels and moved along them; no wall left standing); demo: 1.0 on layout A (video: overhead beside right wrist camera); the same script on layout B: 0.75 (front flap left outside)
